claims.statement: BillCollector.sh is the cron entry point for batch mode: it holds an exclusive non-blocking flock on apps/.bc.lock for the whole docker run (a second start exits 1 with 'already running'), requires a readable apps/.env, mounts .env/Downloads/db into the billcollector:latest image, and runs python3 ./BillCollector.py <ini> [debug].

WebRetriDoc in apps/BillCollector.py is the batch entry point: it vets the vault API with pinned_api_url, requires bitwarden_api_check_status to report 'unlocked', and posts a /sync; any preflight failure exits the process with code 1 before any service runs.

Batch runs iterate the [Playwright] sections of the INI file (with an optional --service <NAME> filter), resolve each '<service> <user>' vault item, and call retrieve_from_service_with_playwright per pair; a failed pair sets failed and continues with the next pair, and the process exits 1 at the end if any pair failed, 0 otherwise.
The second positional argument of BillCollector.py is a valued debug switch: '1'/'true'/'debug' and similar turn headed debug mode on, while 'False'/'0'/'no'/'off' keep it off.

Besides the wrapper-level flock, the batch process calls acquire_run_lock() in apps/helpers/BillCollectorHelpers.py, a non-blocking exclusive flock on apps/.bc.lock, so overlapping cron starts, UI runs, and debug sessions are refused inside the process as well.

retrieve_from_service_with_playwright in apps/BillCollectorServices_pw.py returns True only when the run completed without aborting and at least one file was downloaded successfully; perform_actions drives a sync_playwright persistent Chromium context (headless=not bcs.dbg), sorts and executes the recipe steps, and records a PageState row per step.

In the batch step loop, a non-graceful step failure raises StepAbortError and aborts the run, while a graceful: true step records the error on its PageState and the run continues; expect_download steps execute their nested steps inside page.expect_download().

DatabaseManager in apps/BillCollectorServices_pw.py maintains the legacy schema in apps/db/bc.db: a Service registry table plus one PageStatus_<service>_RunN table per run (created via create_service_run_table), and a finally block calls finalize_service_run so every started service run ends with a terminal success/failure result even when the run is aborted.

billcollector/cli.py main() exposes two subcommands: serve (host from BC_UI_HOST with default 127.0.0.1, default port 8000) and run <task_id> [--debug]; run delegates to runner.run_task and returns its exit code.

serve first runs database.import_ini(config.INI_FILES), a one-time import of the INI [Playwright] sections into Tasks that only runs while the Task table is empty (imported tasks are created disabled with the default monthly cron '0 0 1 * *'), then seeds the UI password hash and calls ui_app.start(); NiceGUI and Playwright are lazy-imported so each subcommand loads only what it needs.

ui/app.py start() wires the daemon: Database, Orchestrator(db), and TaskScheduler(db, orchestrator.start_run); startup runs orchestrator.cleanup_orphans() then scheduler.start(), and shutdown stops the scheduler first (so no new job can dispatch) before orchestrator.shutdown(); ui.run runs with show=False.

TaskScheduler mirrors the Task table into an APScheduler AsyncIOScheduler with a SQLAlchemy jobstore in the same bc.db file - the Task table is the source of truth and the jobstore is a cache; one cron job per enabled task (id task-<id>) targets the module-level _task_job which awaits start_run, and resync()/sync_task() rebuild jobs from task changes.

Orchestrator.start_run is the single run entry for scheduler jobs and UI actions: it claims the task with the atomic claim_task_run (skipping tasks already running/waiting), acquires the global max_concurrency semaphore (default 1), spawns the runner as python -m billcollector run <task_id> in its own session, and hands off monitoring to a separate asyncio task.

The runner subprocess is spawned with start_new_session=True so it leads its own process group: the display-stack children share that group (daemon shutdown can killpg the whole stack), and a SIGKILLed daemon orphans live runners instead of killing them - startup cleanup_orphans then takes over.

The runner finalizes its own Run row with the authoritative result (success/failure/cancelled/needs_attention/interrupted) and normally releases the task to idle; the orchestrator's _finalize_run only closes rows the runner left open (exit 0 -> success, negative signal exit -> interrupted, other non-zero -> failure with the output tail appended to Run.notes), and releases the task when the runner died before creating its row.

Orchestrator lifecycle edges: cleanup_orphans (startup) marks leftover active runs whose pid is dead as interrupted, force-removes their stale display lock, and releases the task to idle; shutdown (SIGTERM) SIGTERMs each live runner's process group then SIGKILLs after 5 s; stop_run (UI Stop) does the same for one task after 10 s.

runner.run_task(task_id, debug) loads the Task, validates the recipe, allocates an Xvfb display via display.allocate_display (atomic O_EXCL lockfile registry) and starts the runner-owned Xvfb/x11vnc/websockify stack, creates the Run row recording its own pid, runs _vault_preflight (pinned local API, unlocked status), executes the recipe in a headful persistent per-task browser profile, and always tears down the display stack and finalizes the Run row; it returns exit code 0 only for result success, 1 otherwise.

Daemon steps re-execute up to MAX_STEP_ATTEMPTS = 3 times (graceful steps are single-attempt), and each step records exactly one PageStatus row plus a per-run screenshot; every downloaded file goes through downloads.track_download, which records sha256, dedups per task via duplicate_of_id, and invokes the CONSUMERS hook slot for non-duplicates.

Stuck runs pause instead of aborting: a non-graceful step that exhausts its attempts, a failed download, or an explicit wait_user step calls pause_loop, which persists a machine-readable pause context on the Run row, flips the task to waiting, pushes an ntfy deep link, and serves the versioned control socket (control.py, PROTOCOL_VERSION 1) from the runner's main thread until resume (re-executes the step), cancel (result=cancelled), or deadline timeout (result=needs_attention).

The daemon UI registers the pages (dashboard, task detail, session, recipe editor, downloads, settings, auth, runfiles) in ui/app.py build_app, and all run actions (Run now, Stop, Run filtered) call orchestrator.start_run / stop_run - the same callbacks the scheduler fires.

billcollector/db.py Database creates the Task/Run/PageStatus/Download/Settings schema in apps/db/bc.db (path overridable via BC_* env vars in config.py) with WAL, busy_timeout=30000, and check_same_thread=False; writers are split by table (orchestrator owns Task/Run lifecycle, runner owns PageStatus/Download, UI owns Task CRUD and Settings) with short writes, and the legacy batch Service / PageStatus_<service>_RunN tables coexist in the same file untouched.

The vault client in billcollector/vault.py plus apps/vault_transport.py is shared by the batch entry point and the daemon runner's _vault_preflight: every request carries explicit timeouts, retries up to VAULT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 on transient failures, raises VaultAPIError (never sys.exit) on final 4xx or exhausted retries, and pinned_api_url requires BW_API_URL to resolve only to local HTTP addresses.

Both modes resolve recipes from git-versioned YAML files named recipe-pw__<service>.yaml (lowercase, spaces as underscores, via config.recipe_path_for) and validate them against recipe-pw-schema.yaml - the batch path and runner via helpers.CheckRecipe, the UI editor via recipes.validate_recipe; runner additionally resolves {{OTP}} to a fresh TOTP at substitution time.

PageState in billcollector/pagestate.py is the interactive-element scan (role, name, locator, bounding-box rect) extracted from BillCollectorServices_pw.py and shared by both step loops; it deliberately imports nothing from Playwright so the lightweight runner subprocess can import it.

Task status is a machine guarded by the atomic claim_task_run row lock (UPDATE ... WHERE status NOT IN ('running','waiting')): idle -> running on claim, running -> waiting during a pause so the scheduler cannot re-trigger, and every finished or interrupted run returns the task to idle.

The runner converts SIGTERM/SIGINT into a RunInterrupted exception raised in its main thread, so a daemon shutdown (or Ctrl+C on the standalone runner) takes the run's full teardown - display-stack reap, Run row finalization as interrupted, and task release to idle - instead of the OS killing the process in place and leaking the display lockfile.

Both operating modes define a successful run with the same contract - the run completed without aborting and at least one file downloaded with result success - with the batch path expressing it as the True/False return of retrieve_from_service_with_playwright and the daemon expressing it as Run.result via run_result, so a completed run with no clean download is a failure in both modes.

Orchestrator lifecycle edges: cleanup_orphans (startup) marks leftover active runs whose pid is dead as interrupted, force-removes their stale display lock, and releases the task to idle; shutdown (SIGTERM) SIGTERMs each live runner's process group, SIGKILLs after the 5 s SHUTDOWN_TIMEOUT, marks rows the runner did not finalize as interrupted, and releases the tasks; stop_run (UI Stop) only signals - SIGTERM to one task's runner group, SIGKILL after the 10 s STOP_TIMEOUT - and leaves finalization to the runner's signal handler or the monitor, so a graceful runner result is never overwritten.
